components.gap: Barwise 1974's original abstract-model-theory axioms (a logic as a syntax functor on a category of languages plus a satisfaction relation obeying the Occurrence, Isomorphism and Translation Axioms, pp. 234-235, with relativization obtained through the Translation Axiom) and his selected Lindstrom formulation (Part II Section 3: Def. 3.1 'as strong as', Thm 3.2, Cor. 3.3, Cor. 3.4 with the Lowenheim property plus either upward LS or countable compactness, pp. 257-259), retaining his actual closure conditions and the stated difference from Lindstrom's notion of logic, are not presented on the handbook route. (An unrouted treatment exists in another packet's file; see defect_observations.)

The route proves only the shared regular-logic theorem. The proofs and prerequisite constructions of Barwise's presentation are not supplied: Theorem 2.2 (Lowenheim property gives Karp property), Theorems 1.2/1.4 (accessibility and the definition of (omega,<)), Theorem 3.2 (L_kappa-omega is as strong as L* iff L* has the Karp property and the well-ordering-number bound) and the Corollary 3.4 derivation including the upward-LS alternative (a), each with his language category, model domain (including his handling of empty/finite models), cardinality and choice hypotheses.

No explicit worked reconstruction and source-to-host notation/statement bridge between Barwise 1974's axioms/Cor. 3.4 and the host regular relational package and thm:p03-lindstrom, preserving Barwise's differing proof route (through the Karp property) and his actual cited/sketched source boundaries (e.g. Karp's theorem referred to an earlier survey), is on the route.

The second edition's distinct full proof and concrete abstract-logic setup are not identified as such.
